INTRODUCTION

Findings from the current reporting period indicate that protection risks affecting displaced populations across Gaza continue to be shaped by 
deepening food insecurity, deteriorating shelter and sanitation conditions, and increasing barriers to accessing humanitarian assistance and essential services. Communities reported growing difficulties in accessing food following the suspension of community kitchens, severe shortages of safe water, worsening environmental health conditions linked to open sewage and infestation, and continued overcrowding in deteriorating shelters. These conditions are contributing to heightened exposure to disease, erosion of dignity, and growing psychosocial distress, particularly among children, older persons, persons with disabilities, and individuals with pre-existing health conditions.

Communities also highlighted increasing challenges related to access to humanitarian assistance, including barriers linked to civil documentation, digital assistance mechanisms, and reduced humanitarian access in areas located near the so-called “yellow” and “orange” lines. At the same time, the presence of explosive remnants of war (ERW) in and around displacement sites continues to pose serious safety risks, particularly for children and communities with limited awareness of reporting and survivor assistance pathways.

The Protection Monitoring System (PMS) continues to provide timely and systematic evidence on protection risks affecting displaced populations across Gaza. Through a combination of 
Key Informant Interviews (KIIs)
 and 
Focus Group Discussions (FGDs)
, the system captures both quantitative trends and qualitative community perspectives to inform protection analysis and response planning. Community feedback during this reporting period highlights increasing reliance on 
negative and constrained coping mechanisms, including reduced food consumption, growing debt, and greater dependence on humanitarian assistance and informal support networks to meet basic needs amid prolonged displacement and deteriorating living conditions. This snapshot presents an overview of protection risk severity scores, evolving risk trends since the start of monitoring in 
August 2024
, and key protection concerns raised by affected communities during the most recent reporting period.

related.title: Missiles and negotiations: Iran 100 days into the war with US and Israel
related.summary: Tehran, Iran – Iranian authorities remain defiant 100 days into the war launched by the United States and Israel as no lasting resolution appears in sight, and civilians bear the brunt of a conflict that has roiled global markets. But the institutions of the Islamic Republic survived and remain in power, as do many officials, including leaders of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), who have continued to heavily disrupt the flow of energy and goods through the Strait of Hormuz while fighting off the US blockade of Iran’s ports.
bullets: Tehran, Iran – Iranian authorities remain defiant 100 days into the war launched by the United States and Israel as no lasting resolution appears in sight, and civilians bear the brunt of a conflict that has roiled global markets.

But the institutions of the Islamic Republic survived and remain in power, as do many officials, including leaders of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), who have continued to heavily disrupt the flow of energy and goods through the Strait of Hormuz while fighting off the US blockade of Iran’s ports.

After roughly 40 days of intense war and thousands of strikes, followed by months of tense “ceasefire” that has now included overnight exchanges of fire for more than a week, an interim deal to reopen the strategic waterway has not materialised.

‘Missiles, not negotiations’ On Sunday, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Tehran hosted Pakistan’s interior minister, the mediating country which itself was hosting an envoy from Lebanon, in an attempt to bridge gaps over Hezbollah and other issues with the US.

In an editorial on Sunday marking the 100-day milestone, the hardline Keyhan newspaper, whose editor-in-chief was appointed by Ali Khamenei, said the experience has taught the system that “America retreated because of missiles, not negotiations”.
related.excerpt: Tehran, Iran – Iranian authorities remain defiant 100 days into the war launched by the United States and Israel as no lasting resolution appears in sight, and civilians bear the brunt of a conflict that has roiled global markets. On the streets of the capital, Tehran, most shops are open, although not with as many customers as before. Traffic has been restored, but only partially, since millions of jobs have either been suspended or eliminated after nationwide protests, aerial bombardment and two state-imposed internet shutdowns over the past several months.
